content: During the initial comprehensive medical evaluation, healthcare providers confirm the diagnosis of diabetes and determine its classification, whether it is type 1, type 2, or another form of diabetes. They also assess the patient for any existing complications related to diabetes and evaluate their overall health status. Providers identify the patient’s social support systems, including family, friends, and community resources, to understand how these networks might assist in managing diabetes effectively. A thorough review of the patient’s medical history is conducted, focusing on previous treatments and risk factors. This includes examining family history, lifestyle factors, and any known complications associated with diabetes. Therapeutic goals are collaboratively established with the patient, taking into account their individual preferences and specific needs. A personalized care plan is then developed, which may include recommendations for lifestyle modifications, strategies for medication management, and a structured plan for ongoing follow-up care.
